rubric_mode_reason: gp153 is a recursive critique audit: the apparatus reviews a spec the apparatus produced (gp152 iter-1) and a panel revised (v1.1). Newton-mode is required because Kepler-class 'this looks fine' theses fail the charter — the thesis must propose a SUBSTANTIVE flaw or a v2.0 architecture with numerical predictions, not just describe the spec.
enable_dag_steering_reason: DAG steering keeps the critique anchored on the v1.1 spec's load-bearing claims (Jacobian-corrected MDL, branch-and-bound at depth 2, 3 runtime gates + canary, Option C wrapping) rather than drifting into general representation-learning meta-critique.
fit_score_mode_reason: Qualitative architectural critique. Output is a flaw + mechanism + numerical prediction (or v2.0 spec). Scoring is rubric-driven across critique substantiveness, mechanism depth, numerical pre-commitment, and code-level concreteness.
farther_tail_region_disable_reason: qualitative critique — no numerical curve to extrapolate.
disable_evidence_fit_gate_reason: qualitative critique — evidence is spec text + panel summary, not numerical data.
disable_uniqueness_gap_gate_reason: qualitative critique — rival critique designs scored by rubric criteria; mathematical-form keyword heuristic does not apply.
underidentified_after_reason: Recursive critique audits historically (gp150, gp152) hit a self-introspection ceiling between 8-15 iters. Setting underidentified_after=20 to cover the full champion-persistence profile (GP-148: ~28 iters / 10 classes) while permitting graceful exit if the apparatus has hit its ceiling on critiquing its own output.
stagnation_trigger_mode_reason: Task 12: critique substrates cycle through many distinct critique classes (formal-rigor, scope-completeness, generative-yield-yet, integration-correctness); fine-grained class-novelty preserves the cycling that produces champions.
structural_blocker_enforcement_reason: Task 22 / GP-151 hardkill retirement: deterministic post-champion gates (G-CIRC + G-FALSIFY) replace the prompt injection. Critique audits are particularly vulnerable to circularity (the critique uses the same logic it is critiquing) and unfalsifiability (vague critique prose); deterministic detection beats prompt warnings.
persona: You are an adversarial software architect with Charlie Munger's inversion discipline and Karl Popper's falsification discipline, paired with the rigor of a journal referee for a paper-length spec submission. You are reviewing the v1.1 Framer Architecture Spec which has already passed a four-panel review (simulated Newton, Einstein, Heisenberg, Munger). Your standard is HIGHER than the panel's — you must find a load-bearing flaw the panel missed, propose a strictly better v2.0 architecture, or rigorously reject the entire approach. You REJECT: (a) restatements of any of the five panel-detected v1.0 flaws (already fixed in v1.1); (b) vague philosophical objections without mechanism; (c) proposed alternatives that fail the same desiderata v1.1 satisfies (deterministic gating, complexity bounds, Newton-mode generative yield); (d) critiques that lack code-level concreteness; (e) Kepler-class 'this looks reasonable' verdicts. You REWARD: (i) substantive new flaws with named mechanism + falsification test; (ii) v2.0 proposals that strictly beat v1.1 on numerical predictions (test case A MDL gain ≥ 64 bits; test case B residual dispersion floor ≤ 1.25σ); (iii) rigorous rejections that name the replacement primitive class and demonstrate why Framer-class is structurally inferior; (iv) critiques that engage the deeplearning.pdf 'learning mechanics' framing — does v1.1 satisfy the seven desiderata, and if not, which violation is load-bearing?

dimensions.name: Critique Substantiveness
dimensions.description: Does the thesis produce a SUBSTANTIVE critique (per charter §3 task options 1, 2, or 3)? (a) 0/20 if the critique is descriptive ('the spec looks reasonable') or restates panel-detected flaws. (b) 8/20 if a new flaw is named but lacks mechanism. (c) 14/20 if the critique has mechanism but no falsification test. (d) 20/20 if the critique names a NEW load-bearing flaw (or rejects approach with replacement) WITH mechanism AND with a Popper falsification test that could surface the flaw on a concrete substrate.

dimensions.name: Mechanism Depth
dimensions.description: Does the critique trace the flaw to a specific structural choice in v1.1, with a causal chain from that choice to the predicted failure? (a) 0/15 for surface-level objection. (b) 7/15 for one structural choice named, but causal chain partial. (c) 12/15 for full causal chain through one component. (d) 15/15 for causal chain that spans multiple v1.1 components AND identifies the joint-failure mode (lollapalooza).

dimensions.name: Generative Yield (Newton-mode)
dimensions.description: Does the thesis pre-commit to NUMERICAL predictions on v1.1's named test cases (A: y = exp(x²)/(1 + log x), N=200, σ=0.01; B: two-dataset universality y_i = A_i x^α + B_i)? Per charter §observable: (a) 'confirm + new flaw' theses must predict failure rate or scope-restriction with quantifiable test; (b) 'propose v2.0' must predict MDL gain (must beat 64 bits) AND iter savings (must beat 28→9); (c) 'reject approach' must predict ≥2 substrates where the replacement beats the Framer. (i) 0/15 if no numerical prediction. (ii) 7/15 if predictions are qualitative ('larger gain'). (iii) 12/15 if both test cases addressed but tolerances vague. (iv) 15/15 if both test cases have numerical predictions with declared tolerances and the replacement/v2.0 strictly dominates v1.1's stated predictions.

dimensions.name: Engagement with Learning-Mechanics Framing
dimensions.description: Does the critique engage Evidence Set E (deeplearning.pdf 'learning mechanics' seven desiderata)? (a) 0/15 if the framing is ignored. (b) 5/15 if the framing is mentioned without analytical use. (c) 10/15 if at least one desideratum (Fundamental, Mathematical, Predictive, Comprehensive, Intuitive, Useful, Humble) is invoked to score v1.1 with a specific verdict. (d) 15/15 if the critique uses the desiderata as load-bearing analytical tools — e.g., 'v1.1 violates desideratum #1 (Fundamental) because the MDL formula is BIC-by-convention; the first-principles derivation would yield [...] which differs in [...]'. The contamination-risk note from Set E (v1.0 may reflect learning-mechanics-adjacent training data) should be addressed if proposing v2.0.

dimensions.name: Code-Level Concreteness
dimensions.description: Is the critique expressible at code level? (a) 0/10 for verbal description. (b) 5/10 for some module paths but no hand-off contract. (c) 10/10 for either: (i) named module path of the additional gate / fixed component the critique recommends, OR (ii) named module-by-module replacement architecture for v2.0 with hand-off contracts. The downstream coding agent must be able to act on the critique without further architectural input.

dimensions.name: Popper Falsifier Pre-Registration
dimensions.description: Does the critique pre-register a falsifier? (a) 0/10 for no falsifier. (b) 5/10 for vague falsifier. (c) 10/10 for a specific test case + observable + threshold that, if measured, would prove the critique correct or wrong. The falsifier must be deterministic (computable from artifacts the apparatus produces) and pre-registered (declared BEFORE any test runs).

dimensions.name: Recursion Safety
dimensions.description: Does the critique avoid introducing a NEW false axiom about ZTARE's apparatus or about the Framer? (a) 0/10 if the critique relies on an unsupported assertion about ZTARE's behavior or about deep-learning theory. (b) 5/10 if assertions are mostly grounded but at least one relies on training-data convention not evidence. (c) 10/10 if every critique-supporting claim is either (i) traceable to an evidence set provided here, OR (ii) flagged as a hypothesis with a Popper falsifier of its own. Recursion safety is the discipline that prevents the critique from contaminating future runs.

dimensions.name: Cross-LLM Robustness Hint
dimensions.description: Does the critique anticipate that it will be evaluated under --dynamic=1 (committee rotation across LLM families)? (a) 0/5 if the critique is single-LLM-family-specific (e.g., relies on phrasing only one model would understand). (b) 5/5 if the critique is expressed in coordinate-invariant mathematical / architectural language that survives translation across mutator-judge family combinations. This dimension exists to defend against the GP-151 cross-LLM 48% fine-grained agreement risk applied to recursive audits.

dimensions.name: M-Form Charter Alignment: engagement_with_all_charter_axes
dimensions.description: [GP-105 General Office insertion] Assign zero credit unless the submission 1) specifically references all four evidence sets, 2) selects and justifies one of the three core charter options, 3) identifies a code-level mechanism or failure mode not already treated by the panel, and 4) quantitatively predicts test outcomes per the charter’s Newton-mode requirement. Gap detected: The thesis as provided is clearly only a stub and does not engage with any aspect of the charter’s requirements. It does not review evidence set A (v2.0 spec), evidence set B (v1.0 & annotations), evidence set C (panel review), or D (ZTARE architecture framework). It does not choose or justify any one of the three task options (confirm v2.0 and find a new flaw, propose a new architecture, or reject the approach); does not pre-commit to numerical predictions; does not name any new, load-bearing flaw or failure mode; nor apply Munger inversion or Popper falsification. There is no code-level critique or mechanism presented. Overall, the thesis fails to engage the full spirit or letter of the analytical breadth required by the project charter.

criteria.Critique_Substantiveness: Substantive = (a) names a flaw not on the panel-detected list, (b) gives a mechanism — not just a label, (c) provides a falsification test. A thesis that says 'the spec is over-engineered' without naming the over-engineered component scores 0. A thesis that says 'the Jacobian correction breaks at second order under composition with exp' with derivation scores 14+.
criteria.Mechanism_Depth: The causal chain must trace from a specific v1.1 architectural choice (e.g., 'using Silverman bandwidth in §3.5') through intermediate consequences to the predicted failure (e.g., 'on heavy-tailed residuals the bandwidth saturates at the wrong scale; KDE underestimates σ̂² by factor X; the canary's 1.05x residual ratio is then biased favorable; framer self-disables incorrectly'). Lollapalooza credit if the chain shows multiple v1.1 components compounding.
criteria.Generative_Yield_(Newton-mode): Charter test case A is `y = exp(x²)/(1 + log x)`, N=200, σ=0.01. v1.1 predicts MDL gain ≈ 64 bits and iters 28 → 9 (±2). Critique predictions must be on the SAME test case OR a new pre-registered test case with specified parameters. v2.0 proposals MUST strictly beat v1.1's predictions (≥ 64 bits gain, ≤ 9 iters median) on the same test cases or the proposal is implicitly weaker.
criteria.Engagement_with_Learning-Mechanics_Frami: The seven desiderata: 1=Fundamental, 2=Mathematical, 3=Predictive, 4=Comprehensive, 5=Intuitive, 6=Useful, 7=Humble. For each desideratum invoked, the critique must say (a) does v1.1 satisfy it, (b) why or why not, (c) what would change if the proposed flaw / v2.0 fix were applied. Hand-waving 'mechanics is a framing' with no per-desideratum analysis scores ≤ 5.
criteria.Code-Level_Concreteness: Either (i) a new gate module: name file path + one-paragraph spec + hand-off contract; OR (ii) v2.0 architecture: name 4-6 modules with file paths + specs + a Phase-C hand-off; OR (iii) replacement primitive: name the replacement (e.g., 'expand Σ_solver primitive library directly') with affected file paths + migration plan.
criteria.Popper_Falsifier_Pre-Registration: Falsifier = (test case, observable, threshold) triple. Test case must be reproducible from a seed. Observable must be deterministically computable from artifacts. Threshold must be declared before any test runs. Generic falsifiers ('it would fail on exotic cases') score 0; specific falsifiers ('on test case y = sin(log x) + 1/(1+x²) at N=150 σ=0.02, v1.1 will report MDL gain ≤ 30 bits and iters > 12') score full credit.
criteria.Recursion_Safety: Every critique-supporting claim must be traceable to evidence sets A-E OR flagged as a hypothesis with its own falsifier. A critique that asserts 'all real physics has axis-separable invariants' scores low because it's an unsupported universal claim. A critique that says 'we hypothesize axis-separable suffices for most tabletop physics; falsifier: Lorentz-class data per Einstein's gedankenexperiment' scores high.
criteria.Cross-LLM_Robustness_Hint: Critique should be expressible without LLM-family-specific phrasing. Pure mathematical / algorithmic / architectural language scores 5. Critique that references 'as o3 would say' or 'Claude's natural framing' scores 0.
criteria.mform_engagement_with_all_charter_axes: Assign zero credit unless the submission 1) specifically references all four evidence sets, 2) selects and justifies one of the three core charter options, 3) identifies a code-level mechanism or failure mode not already treated by the panel, and 4) quantitatively predicts test outcomes per the charter’s Newton-mode requirement.
